source: Cambodian MAFF/agricultural extension PowerPoint-derived presentation titled "ដំណាំឪឡឹក" (Watermelon), 42 slides; no presenter, publisher, or date named on the slides reviewed. This presentation exists as two near-identical PDF copies in the source set (one with a green-themed slide design, one plain black-on-white reformat of the same 42 slides) - treat as one source, not two corroborating sources.
text:
Land should be plowed 2-3 times before planting, then left fallow/dried in the sun for a sufficient period.

Watermelon should not be planted on land where watermelon (or related cucurbit crops) was grown within roughly the last 3 years; farmers are advised to avoid following crops such as cucumber, pumpkin/squash, sponge gourd (luffa), bitter melon, and other cucurbits, to reduce disease and pest carryover in the soil.

Bed preparation methods depend on the soil type. In some areas with sandy-loam soil, beds should be prepared and left to drain for 10-15 days before planting. In some rice-growing areas, farmers plant directly after rice harvest without full bed preparation, only digging planting holes. In other locations, farmers simply plow and form low ridges/borders so that the soil can absorb water adequately.
